commitResults.messageTitle: ListCommand: Reject extra arguments and report an empty register
commitResults.messageBody:
The list command ignores any text after the command word, inherited from
the address book template, and always replies "Listed all equipment."
even when there is nothing to list.

The MVP feature specification in the User Guide requires list to reject
parameters with a usage error and to tell the user when the register is
empty. A coordinator who mistypes `list CAM001` expecting a filtered
result currently gets the full list with no hint that the argument was
dropped, and an empty list gives no feedback at all.

Let's add a ListCommandParser that rejects any non-blank argument with
the usage message, and route the list command word through it. Let's
also make ListCommand reply "No equipment found." when the register has
no equipment to show.

The check lives in a parser, like the other commands, so that argument
validation stays out of execute. The empty-register reply is a normal
result rather than an exception because nothing has gone wrong. The
existing parser and logic tests that asserted the old behaviour are
updated to match.
Update UserGuide to match MVP feature specification
Implement Return Equipment Command

commitResults.messageTitle: Filter command: Add availability filter for equipment
commitResults.messageBody:
Equipment can only be viewed as a full list or searched by name. There
is no way to see which items are free to borrow or which are out on
loan.

Club members need that view when deciding what to lend out or chase
for return. Without it, they have to scan the whole list by hand and
read each item's status.

Let's add a filter command that takes "available" or "issued" in any
letter case and shows only equipment with that status. It reports
"Showing available equipment." or "Showing issued equipment." when
there are matches, and "No available equipment found." or "No issued
equipment found." when there are none. A missing, extra or unsupported
argument is rejected with the usage "filter <available|issued>".

The command applies the status through the existing
Model#updateFilteredEquipmentList, so the equipment panel updates
through the list it already observes, and the existing list command
clears the filter. The parser accepts exactly one argument, like
ReturnCommandParser, so command syntax stays consistent.

This is the command and parsing part of the availability filter. The
filter staying in place when equipment is added is already in master
through #73. Keeping it across issue, return and remove is covered by
the model and integration work, and the DG and UG entries come
separately.
Add integration tests for availability filter command sequences

The parser builds ClearCommand without looking at the arguments, so
"clear CAM001" empties the whole register, issued equipment included,
and saves the empty register to disk.

The User Guide says extra parameters are rejected with a usage error.
Because clear is destructive, accepting a stray argument can wipe real
records on a typo, such as someone meaning to act on one item.

Let's add a ClearCommandParser that rejects any non-blank argument with
a usage error, and route the clear command word through it. The usage
message follows the one list already uses.

The existing parser test asserted that "clear 3" is accepted, which
encodes the bug, so it now expects the usage error. An integration test
checks that a rejected clear leaves both the in-memory register and the
saved file unchanged, and that a plain clear still empties both.

Fixes #80

commitResults.messageTitle: Help and exit commands: Reject extra arguments
commitResults.messageBody:
The parser builds HelpCommand and ExitCommand without looking at the
arguments, so "help extra" opens the help window and "exit extra" quits
the program.

The User Guide says that missing or extra parameters are rejected with
a usage error. Every other command already follows that rule, so help
and exit are the odd ones out, and an exit command that ignores a typo
can end a session the user did not mean to end.

Let's add a HelpCommandParser and an ExitCommandParser that reject any
non-blank argument with a usage error, and route both command words
through them. The usage messages follow the ones list and clear use.

Validating makes the behavior match the existing User Guide, so no
documentation change is needed. The existing parser tests asserted that
"help 3" and "exit 3" are accepted, which encodes the gap, so they now
expect the usage error.

Fixes #86

commitResults.messageTitle: UG: Specify the accepted borrower-name alphabet
commitResults.messageBody:
The User Guide says a borrower name contains "only letters and
spaces", but validation accepts only the ASCII letters A-Z and a-z
plus spaces. A name such as "José" is rejected even though it matches
the guide's plain-language description.

Users cannot predict validation from a rule that is broader than the
one actually enforced, and they only learn the difference from an error
after typing the name.

Let's state the real alphabet in the issue command's name rule, and
name accented and non-English letters as rejected. The existing rules
for the 1-50 character limit and for trimming and combining spaces are
unchanged.

This only clarifies the documentation. Name validation itself is not
changed, so the error message and the behavior stay as they are.

Fixes #88

commitResults.messageTitle: Return command: Add parser for return equipment
commitResults.messageBody:
The app can add, list and remove equipment, but it has no way to
record that issued equipment has been returned.

Returning equipment depends on the issue command's borrower field,
which is not yet on master. Parsing the command input does not depend
on it, so it can be built and reviewed separately now.

Let's add ReturnCommandParser, which accepts exactly one equipment ID
and validates it with the same EquipmentId rules used by add and
remove. Let's also register the return command word in
AddressBookParser and add a placeholder ReturnCommand whose execute
reports that the command is not yet supported without touching the
model.

Reusing EquipmentId keeps ID validation and case-insensitive matching
consistent across commands, as the feature spec requires. The parser
mirrors RemoveCommandParser so that both single-ID commands behave the
same way on missing or extra arguments.

The errors for equipment that does not exist or is not currently
issued depend on the model and will be added with the return logic.

commitResults.messageTitle: Return command: Mark issued equipment as returned
commitResults.messageBody:
The return command parses an equipment ID, but executing it only
reports that the command is not yet supported. Issued equipment
therefore cannot be made available again.

Returning equipment is a must-have feature. Without it, every issued
item stays issued forever and can never be issued to anyone else.

Let's add Equipment#markReturned, which returns an available copy with
no borrower, and let ReturnCommand use it to replace the issued record
in the model. Let's reject the command when the equipment does not
exist or is not currently issued, using the error messages from the
feature specification.

markReturned mirrors Equipment#issueTo so that both status transitions
live on the immutable Equipment record and keep its status and
borrower consistent. The lookup and validation are extracted into a
helper so that execute stays at a single level of abstraction.

The tests were written before the implementation. Besides unit tests
for the command and model, an integration test checks that a return
is saved and that a rejected return leaves the saved data unchanged.
The UG gains a section and a command summary row for return.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: UG: Rewrite for the ClubLogistics MVP commands
commitResults.messageBody:
The UG still describes AddressBook Level 3. It documents contact
commands such as edit, find, delete and clear, and only partly covers
the equipment commands, with a note that some of them operate on
contacts.

Users of ClubLogistics only track equipment, so the contact material
is misleading, and the UG does not tell them the rules and error
messages of the MVP commands.

Let's rewrite the UG around the MVP feature specification. Let's
document add, remove, list, issue and return with their formats,
parameter rules, examples, successful outputs and error messages,
describe the equipment record and its statuses, and drop the contact
commands, help and the AB3 screenshot.

The equipment ID rules are shared by every command, so they are stated
once and referenced by each command instead of being repeated. Error
messages are presented as tables so that users can quickly match a
message to its cause.

The UG follows the specification, which the code does not fully match
yet. For example, list does not show each item's status or reject
extra parameters. These gaps will be addressed in separate changes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Equipment card: Add color-coded status indicator
commitResults.messageBody:
Equipment cards show the status only as text, such as "Available" or
"Issued to: John Tan".

Users scanning a long equipment list have to read every status line to
find what is free to issue. A visual cue lets them spot available and
issued items at a glance.

Let's add a small circle beside the status text, colored green for
available equipment and orange for issued equipment.

The colors are applied through CSS style classes rather than set in
Java, so the palette can be adjusted in DarkTheme.css without touching
the card logic. The style class is chosen with an exhaustive switch on
EquipmentStatus, so adding a new status will fail compilation until it
is given a color.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: AGENTS.md: Align commit conventions with CS2103 standards
commitResults.messageBody:
AGENTS.md describes a commit message style that differs from the
CS2103 Standards/Conventions and the SE-EDU Git conventions they link
to. It forbids bullet points, makes "Let's" mandatory and omits the
subject line rules.

Commits that follow the project instructions may therefore violate the
course standards that the project is assessed against.

Let's rewrite the commit message section to mirror the SE-EDU
conventions, covering the subject length limit, imperative mood,
capitalization, body structure, branch naming and examples.

Linking both source pages keeps the rules traceable to the official
standard. The DG/UG abbreviation rule is kept as it is project-specific
and does not conflict with the standard.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Equipment filtering: Adding items resets the active filter

commitResults.messageTitle: JsonUtil: Reject null JSON documents when reading
commitResults.messageBody:
A data or preferences file containing only the JSON literal `null`
deserializes to a null object, which readJsonFile passes to
Optional.of. The resulting NullPointerException escapes startup,
which only catches DataLoadingException, so the existing recovery
path is bypassed and the app crashes.

A null document carries no usable data, so it should be treated
like any other invalid file: an empty register for equipment data,
and default preferences for user preferences.

Let's,
* throw DataLoadingException from readJsonFile when the document
  is null, so both storage readers inherit the check
* make MainApp#initModelManager protected, matching initPrefs, so
  startup recovery can be tested directly
* add regression tests for JsonUtil, both storage readers and both
  startup recovery paths

Rejecting the document in JsonUtil, rather than in each storage
class, keeps one check for every JSON file the app loads.

Fixes #81

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: UG, DG: Document equipment status in the data file
commitResults.messageBody:
The UG and DG describe each saved equipment record as holding only
`id`, `name` and `issuedTo`, with status derived from the borrower.
Saved records also contain `status`, and the loader rejects the whole
register when `status` and `issuedTo` disagree.

A user following the UG who clears only `issuedTo` on an issued item
gets an invalid file, so ClubLogistics starts with an empty register,
and the next command can overwrite the rejected file.

Let's,
* add `status` to the UG data file example
* list the two valid status/borrower combinations, and tell users to
  update both fields together, with a worked example
* explain that a missing `status` is inferred from the borrower only
  for compatibility with older files
* correct the DG storage section to describe the persisted `status`,
  the consistency check and the compatibility inference

Fixes #83

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: UG: Tell users to close the app before editing data
commitResults.messageBody:
The UG invites users to edit the data file and to transfer records
by replacing it, but does not say to close ClubLogistics first.

ClubLogistics loads the register only at startup and saves it after
every successful command. Edits or a transferred file written while
the app is running are silently overwritten by the next command,
even a read-only one such as `list`.

Let's,
* explain why the app must be closed, and add a back up, close,
  edit, restart procedure to the data file section
* rewrite the data transfer FAQ as the same procedure, covering the
  instances on both computers

The procedure sits after the existing caution box, away from the
data file schema, so it does not overlap the schema fix for #83.

Fixes #84

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Update storage class diagram for equipment data
commitResults.messageBody:
The storage class diagram still shows the AB3 contact adapters
JsonAdaptedPerson and JsonAdaptedTag, and the rendered PNG still
shows the AddressBook storage classes. The DG lists it among the
diagrams that do not yet match the code.

Readers of the DG get a storage design that no longer exists, and
the PlantUML source and PNG disagree with each other.

Let's,
* replace the contact and tag adapters with JsonAdaptedEquipment,
  shown with its persisted fields id, name, status and issuedTo
* keep the Storage realization and StorageManager's delegation to
  JsonUserPrefsStorage and JsonClubLogisticsStorage
* regenerate the PNG from the updated source
* embed the diagram with a caption in the Storage component section,
  at its natural width, and drop it from the list of unadapted
  diagrams

The inner UserPrefs and ClubLogistics packages are removed. Each held
a single storage path, so they repeated the class names, and in the
rendered image their titles overlapped the "1" multiplicities.

The PNG is rendered with PlantUML 1.2024.7 using its built-in
Smetana layout, as Graphviz is not available on this machine.

Fixes #106

commitResults.messageTitle: FileUtil: Retry atomic replacement while Windows denies access
commitResults.messageBody:
Saves write a temporary file and atomically move it over the data
file. Windows refuses that move while any other process has the data
file open, and reports AccessDeniedException.

On Windows, antivirus scanners, sync clients such as OneDrive, and
search indexing briefly open files, so a save can fail at random with
a misleading "insufficient permissions" error even though nothing is
wrong. The same behaviour makes
FileUtilTest.writeToFile_repeatedReplacement_readersSeeOnlyCompleteVersions
fail on every Windows run, so the windows-latest CI job cannot pass.

Let's retry the move up to 20 times, 25 ms apart, when access is
denied, and fail immediately when the destination is a directory,
since waiting cannot fix that case.

A bounded retry keeps the existing atomic, no-fallback guarantee: the
data file is still never truncated or written in place. The total
delay of about half a second is only paid when a save would otherwise
fail. macOS and Linux replace open files directly, so their behaviour
is unchanged.

A deterministic test holds the data file open briefly to reproduce the
Windows behaviour without relying on thread timing.

Fixes #146

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
